text:
miguel: Quick RFC follow-up — idea: introduce a small "preempt window" token on ingress connections so Frontdoor can request a graceful revoke of long-running or over-budget streams. Thinking about tradeoffs and how it fits with hedging/late-bind.

anna: sketch the happy path? not sure i follow the token semantics.

miguel: happy path: Frontdoor accepts OPEN, marks connection preemptable, mints a signed token T with expiry + epoch, injects `x-rw-preempt: T` to upstream. If capacity pressure or tenant revoke needed, Frontdoor emits a REVOKE event (id + epoch). Upstream treats REVOKE as a soft signal first, then hard-cut after drain timeout.

sam: naive flow looks like this:
```
Client -> Frontdoor: OPEN {id, tenant, preemptable: true}
Frontdoor -> Client: ACK (id, T)
Frontdoor -> Upstream: request + headers { x-rw-preempt: T }
...streaming...
Frontdoor -> Upstream: REVOKE {id, epoch} // soft revoke first
Upstream: finish current in-flight tokens or close after drain_timeout
```

irene: couple of immediate concerns: 1) idempotency & side effects if we cut mid-stream, 2) interaction with hedging and late binding (we might have multiple concurrent upstreams for same request).

sam: for hedging we can include epoch+nonce in token so only the intended upstream honors the revoke; other hedged inflight copies ignore unless token epoch matches. but that means we need consistent token propagation on fanouts.

anna: security: tokens must be signed (HMAC) and short-lived. otherwise a rogue upstream could fake REVOKE. example token header format: `T = base64(hdr|expiry|epoch|hmac)`

irene: observability: we should emit a span event `revoked=true/soft` and counters for `revoke.soft`, `revoke.hard`, `revoke.expired`. also log tenant + quota-bucket.

miguel: ops questions: how do we avoid thrashing when many tenants hit revoke? do we randomize drain_timeout or use backoff windows per-tenant? Also cost: adding preempt checks may add per-request CPU.

ops-bot: simulated revoke sweep executed at 15:17 UTC; 0 upstream 5xx observed; avg drain latency 220ms. :white_check_mark:

sam: implementation note: prefer opaque token (no remote KV per revoke) — frontdoor signs token so gateways don't need to consult control plane for every revoke. keep a compact revoke bitmap when hard-revoking recent epochs.

anna: prototype plan: i'll draft token shape + verification snippet and a tiny frontdoor lib. quick pseudo-hmac: `h = HMAC(key, id|expiry|epoch)` -> `T = base64(id|expiry|epoch|h)`.

miguel: tradeoffs summary i wrote down:
- Pros: can reclaim capacity without immediate hard-kill; keeps graceful UX for streaming apps.
- Cons: more complex token lifecycle, hedging coordination, marginal CPU cost, and harder debugging if epochs mismatch.

irene: +1 on adding tracer events. also recommend a canary with tenant-scoped revokes only.

miguel: next steps: i'll open RFC PR with sequence diagrams, cost perf estimate, and proposed headers. @anna can you prototype token format by EOW? @sam please sketch hedging interaction in the PR.

anna: on it. EOW target. :thumbsup:

sam: will add hedging sketch.

ops-bot: reminder: create RFC issue link when ready.
